clue.text: Risk irregular pulse action

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of these two words fall in no fixed order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor gambles on what an irregular heartbeat means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges PULSE and ACTION together into the eleven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculation is a financial venture taken on chance, a form of gamble.

clue.text: Rowing boat for one

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A small craft built to carry a single oarsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay outrigger craft that can be paddled or sailed.

clue.text: Rebuked, leader of Commons lay low

indicators.note: leader of points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to lie low is to hide, so lay low gives hid

explanation.surface: After being told off, the head of the House of Commons kept out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay low' is the past tense of lie low, matching the past tense HID.
explanation.definitionFit: Chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold or reprimand.

clue.text: Envoy and member dined

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
dined means ate

explanation.surface: A diplomat and a club member had dinner together.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is a papal or official ambassador sent on a mission.

clue.text: Can get into Russian currency and stock, with bad times on the way

indicators.note: get into places the currency inside the word for a can, splitting it open

parts.note: a can is a tin
the rouble is the currency of Russia
stock is a store of goods

explanation.surface: Someone converts savings into roubles and shares and foresees hard times ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link to the definition; T(ROUBLES)IN gives the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means difficulties are coming in the future.

clue.text: A number of animals in the pound

definitions.text: A number of animals in the pound

parts.words: A number of animals in the pound
parts.note: reads like stray creatures held in a dog pound, but means both big cats (snow leopards) and the sixteen weight units that make up a pound

explanation.surface: Several strays are locked up at the animal pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called the ounce, and sixteen of the weight units make an avoirdupois pound.

clue.text: Abandoned in disarray behind unit I infiltrated

indicators.note: infiltrated says the single letter gets in among the other letters
in disarray means the letters of these words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier left behind his scattered unit after enemy agents got in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' rearranges BEHIND and UNIT, and 'infiltrated' puts I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, free of inhibitions.

clue.text: Record grades he contrived to get. at this are in dispute.

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: contrived means the letters of these words are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A clerk fiddles the recorded marks, and a row follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges GRADES HE into GERHEADS. The definition reads as a fill-in: those at this are in dispute, as people at odds are said to be.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at odds' with this word describes parties locked in a quarrel.

clue.text: Prepare for take-off

parts.note: reads as readying an aircraft, but means unfastening clothes before removing them

explanation.definitionFit: Unfastening buttons or a zip is what one does before removing a garment.

clue.text: Paying a visit when the operation 'is over

definitions.meaning: dropping in on someone at their home
regaining consciousness after anaesthetic once surgery ends

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both calling on someone and recovering consciousness after being knocked out or anaesthetised.

clue.text: Intimate there's a rejection of butter substitute

indicators.note: a rejection throws the word back, so the letters run in reverse order

parts.note: in the economic slogan 'guns or butter', weapons are the alternative to butter

explanation.surface: A cosy diner turns away margarine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'guns versus butter' choice in economics is between military and civilian spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug describes a cosy, close, private place, like an intimate room.

clue.text: Whine about odd skin blemish left from rash

annotationWithheld.why: Whine about odd skin blemish left from rash: HUM around RUM and SCAR gives everything but the A in HARUMSCARUM, and no clue word supplies it
annotationWithheld.clue: Whine about odd skin blemish left from rash

clue.text: Watch parts of a gymnastic performance

definitions.text: Watch parts of a gymnastic performance

parts.words: Watch parts of a gymnastic performance
parts.note: reads as viewing a routine, but hands and springs are also parts of a timepiece

explanation.surface: A spectator catches some sections of a floor routine.
explanation.definitionFit: These are acrobatic moves in which the gymnast vaults over onto the hands and back to the feet.

clue.text: Where string is kept

parts.note: sounds like a drawer for twine, but a string is a trainer's set of racehorses

explanation.definitionFit: Racehorses in a trainer's string are housed in these buildings and the yard around them.

clue.text: Has lost Russian fighter in a way that's humiliating

annotationWithheld.why: Has lost Russian fighter in a way that's humiliating: anagram of HAS plus MIG gives all of SHAMING but the N, and no clue word supplies it
annotationWithheld.clue: Has lost Russian fighter in a way that's humiliating

clue.text: Teased about daughter being given a tranquilliser

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl who was mocked had to be calmed with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedated describes someone calmed by a dose of a soothing drug.

clue.text: Dad, getting back pain is brave

indicators.note: getting back says the word for father is turned to run backwards

parts.note: pa is a word for father
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A father with back trouble is being courageous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' turns PA into AP. 'brave' is a noun here, a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people, and a brave is a warrior of such a people.

clue.text: Superior rose in plot

indicators.note: plot is a verb meaning to scheme or rearrange, telling us to reorder the letters

explanation.surface: A higher-ranking gardener sees a rose growing in the flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a garden bed but rearranges ROSE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior is someone of higher rank or standing.

clue.text: Contained when amount's inverted erroneously

indicators.note: erroneously means wrongly placed, so the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A sum was kept under wraps because a figure had been printed upside down by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erroneously' rearranges AMOUNTS and INVERTED; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Contained in the sense of reserved, keeping one's feelings in check.

clue.text: See us return before long, to flat

indicators.note: return sends the word back, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit soon before moving into an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns US into SU. 'See' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on one's back.

clue.text: Hesitate to dig out the animal

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
to mine is to dig out ore

explanation.surface: Pausing before excavating an animal from its burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The ermine is the stoat, especially in its white winter coat.

clue.text: Top workers' group in Southend given notice

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for a gathering of workers

parts.note: a bee is a group gathered to work, as in a sewing bee
the end of the word South is H
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A union delegation in the seaside town of Southend is handed redundancy notices.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend is an Essex seaside town, but here it means the end of 'South'. 'Top' is a verb, to cut off the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for executing them, as decapitation does.

clue.text: Seen to be within one's grasp

parts.note: the infinitive to be gives be
something within one's grasp is held

explanation.surface: Something visible seems close enough to reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past participle of behold, to look upon.

clue.text: Followed and seized

definitions.meaning: understood an argument, kept up with it
took hold of firmly with the hand

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both took hold of physically and understood mentally.

clue.text: A duck that's blue

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero, nil

explanation.surface: A depressed-looking duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter out without scoring makes a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it.

clue.text: A physical handicap? I'm breaking a record!

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the outer word open to put the other inside

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
taken as written

explanation.surface: An athlete with an injury still sets a new best.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an athletic triumph despite an injury; 'breaking' is the container signal, with the record cut open.
explanation.definitionFit: A limp is an uneven gait from an injured leg, a physical impediment.

clue.text: A number of militiamen or just one

definitions.meaning: a body of soldiers forming a single formation
a single thing, the number one

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a military detachment and a single item or the number one.

clue.text: Ordered inside to bed for being naughty

indicators.note: ordered here means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child is sent to bed for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a parent's command but rearranges INSIDE TO BED; 'for being' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A naughty child is one who will not obey.

clue.text: Egg on some courgettes

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Encouraging a cook to add some vegetable marrows.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to push or spur them, to press them forward.

clue.text: Tiny Eastern spider, weaving — being lucky to have this facility

definitions.text: being lucky to have this facility

indicators.note: weaving means the letters are interlaced into a new order, as a spider spins

explanation.surface: A small spider from the Orient spins its web and happens upon good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaving' rearranges TINY, E and SPIDER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is the knack of making happy discoveries by chance.
